memo.design-capture.body: Capture a fleeting architecture decision at the moment it appears. Preserve the original note as authority, then connect later interpretations instead of rewriting the source.
memo.design-capture.comment: A useful follow-up records why the decision matters and what evidence could make us revisit it.

rss.deep-modules.feed_description: Practical writing about keeping software understandable as it grows.
rss.deep-modules.item_title: Deep modules hide complexity behind small interfaces
rss.deep-modules.summary: A deep module spends internal complexity to make its public surface easier to learn and harder to misuse.
rss.deep-modules.article: Deep modules are valuable because a small, stable interface can conceal substantial implementation detail. The design succeeds when callers need to understand fewer decisions, invariants, and failure branches. Depth is not the same as size: a large module with a broad, leaky interface is still shallow.

atom.peer-discovery.feed_description: Small architectural patterns for cooperating runtime peers.
atom.peer-discovery.summary: Peers can advertise exact capabilities and liveness while domain callers keep request semantics in their own managers.
atom.peer-discovery.article: Service discovery answers which live peer claims an exact capability. Invocation remains a separate protocol operation. A routing layer can select an eligible peer without teaching the generic peer subsystem the business meaning of the capability payload.
